rationale: The workflow runs on every push to all branches and never cancels superseded in-progress runs. Pattern P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (stale_run_cancellation) supports canceling older runs for the same workflow+branch when a newer revision supersedes them, reducing duplicate CI work (reported vm_time reduction ~1.9% free / 4.1% paid). Preconditions are met: runs share the same workflow and branch, and a newer push supersedes older checks. Contraindications are not triggered: this is a check, not release/deployment work, and grouping by `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` isolates distinct branches. The change uses native GitHub Actions `concurrency` with `cancel-in-progress: true`—no new action, secret, permission change, or network access—and preserves all existing steps and coverage, since the latest run per branch still completes fully.
